t: You're at the Museum of Comedy, which is both a museum of comedic history and a venue. It was founded by Martin Witts, a theatre director born in 1962. That background fits the place, because it works as a living space for performance as well as a collection about comedy's past. Witts matters here simply because he started it, and the idea of pairing history with a working stage comes from him. I don't have further details about what's on display or what's on tonight, so I'll leave those for you to discover.
